title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
prompt: Given an array `nums` of `n` integers where `nums[i]` is in the range `[1, n]`, return an array of all the integers in the range `[1, n]` that do not appear in `nums`. Solve it without using extra space (other than the output array) and in `O(n)` time — you may mutate the input array.

examples.explanation: Every value from 1 to n already appears exactly once, so no numbers are missing and the result is empty.

hints: A set of seen values gives O(n) time but O(n) extra space. Since values are bounded to [1, n], can the array itself store which values were seen?
Each value v in nums can be paired with index v-1. What if visiting a value left a 'mark' at that index?
For each number, negate the value at the index it points to (abs(num) - 1). Indices whose values remain positive at the end were never pointed to, meaning that index+1 is missing.

solution.approach: Since every value is in [1, n], each value v can be mapped to index v - 1. Walk the array and for each value, negate whatever is stored at its mapped index (using the absolute value to avoid re-reading an already-negated entry). After this pass, any index whose value is still positive was never 'pointed to' by any element, meaning index + 1 never appeared in the array. Collecting those indices gives the missing numbers using only the input array as storage.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra space, excluding the output array
